{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Use Philippine English|date=May 2023}} {{Use mdy dates|date=May 2023}} [[File:Ph fil congress districts manila.png|thumb|Legislative districts of Manila]] {{Politics of the Philippines}} The [[highly urbanized city]] of [[Manila]] is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] by its '''six congressional districts'''. Every three years, each district elects one representative who will sit on their behalf in Congress. In addition, each district is allotted six seats in the [[Manila City Council]], with councilors being elected every three years. == History == Areas now under the jurisdiction of Manila were initially represented as part of the [[Manila's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the [[Manila (province)|province of Manila]] in the [[Malolos Congress]] from 1898 to 1899; the district [[1898 Philippine legislative election|elected]] [[#1898–1899|four representatives]]. The city of Manila, chartered in 1901, first gained separate representation in 1907. It was initially divided into two [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|representative districts]] from 1907 to 1949. When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the city formed part of the [[Philippines's 4th senatorial district|fourth senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member Senate. In the disruption caused by the [[World War II|Second World War]], Manila was incorporated into the [[City of Greater Manila]] on January 1, 1942, through [[Manuel Quezon]]'s Executive Order No. 400 as a wartime emergency measure. Greater Manila was represented by [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the city mayor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a citywide assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, Manila's pre-war two-district representation was retained; this remained so until 1949. By virtue of the ''Revised Charter of the City of Manila'',{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=409|title=An Act to Revise the Charter of the City of Manila, and for Other Purposes|author=Congress of the Philippines|date=June 18, 1949|access-date=June 13, 2016|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/republicacts/republicactno409.html}} enacted on June 18, 1949, the city was divided into four congressional districts. The city elected four representatives from the [[2nd Congress of the Philippines|2nd Congress]] up to the [[7th Congress of the Philippines|7th Congress]]. The city was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV]] from 1978 to 1984, and elected [[#1984–1986|six representatives]], at large, to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Manila was reapportioned into six [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional districts]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|access-date=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987. It elected members to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine House of Representatives elections|that same year]]. == Current districts == The city was last apportioned upon the proclamation of the [[Constitution of the Philippines|1987 Constitution]], where it was granted six seats in Congress. The city's current congressional delegation composes of five members of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]], and one member of the [[Nationalist People's Coalition]]; five members are also members of the [[Asenso Manileño]] local party.
